title: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian regular schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-regular-scheme]. On each component suppose the codimension is $c\geq0$ and the ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $c$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. On ordinary small-etale derived categories with Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], the Kummer-supported fundamental-class morphism of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism:
$$\eta_{i,n}:\Lambda_{n,Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}(c)[2c].$$
Equivalently, $i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}$ has its sole cohomology sheaf in degree $2c$, canonically $\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)$. Here $i_n^!$ is the right adjoint of ordinary etale $Ri_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. No excellence, field-of-definition, or smoothness-over-a-field hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorem 3.1.1, applied to Noetherian regular pairs and the class of Definition 2.3.1; no excellence assumption in that theorem.

proof.text: Reduce first to coefficients $A_1=\mathbf F_\ell$. Fix the original pair and work where $c$ is constant. For the actual supported maps $\eta_r$, use the cones $C_r$ of [lem-per-gysin-coefficient-cone-triangles]. Suppose $C_1=0$. Induct on $r$: for $r\geq2$ the supplied distinguished triangle is $C_{r-1}\to C_r\to C_1\to C_{r-1}[1]$. Assuming $C_{r-1}=0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](ii) with $W=C_r$ and $a=1_{C_r}$. Its composite to $C_1=0$ vanishes, so the identity factors through $C_{r-1}=0$ and is zero. Thus $C_r$ is a zero object. By [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] on the cone triangle of $\eta_r$, this is equivalent to $\eta_r$ being an isomorphism. The same criterion at $r=1$ starts the induction from purity over $\mathbf F_\ell$. This uses compatible representatives of the supported maps; it does not assume that exceptional pullback commutes with a derived change of coefficient rings.

We now prove punctual purity over $\mathbf F_\ell$ for every regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible. By [lem-per-punctual-purity-trait-test], it suffices to treat an integral regular scheme $V$ flat and quasi-projective of finite type over a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait $S$ with $\ell$ invertible. This reduction includes completion and the equal-characteristic case; it does not require the original $X$ or $Z$ to be excellent. Fix such $S,V$.

source.place: XVI section 3.7, first paragraph, p.254, with Propositions 3.2.4--3.2.5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-trait-prime-to-ell-log-alteration] to $V/S$. It gives a finite trait extension $T/S$ and a projective dominant generically finite etale map $f:Y\to V$ of degree $d>0$ prime to $\ell$, with $Y$ integral regular and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$, carrying an fs log structure log smooth over $T$. Since $\ell$ is a unit on $S$, it remains a unit on $T$. The log-smooth purity theorem [lem-per-log-smooth-trait-punctual-purity] therefore makes $Y$ punctually pure over $\mathbf F_\ell$. We use the geometric alteration theorem here, without assuming purity of $V$ or of any non-log-smooth alteration.

Use [lem-per-punctual-purity-proper-degree-descent] for $f:Y\to V$ over $S$. Both schemes are integral regular, finite type and quasi-projective over $S$ by the alteration statement; its projective map is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], its generic degree is $d$, and $d$ is invertible in $\mathbf F_\ell$ since $\ell\nmid d$. The lemma requires no flatness of $f$. It follows that $V$ is punctually pure. This verifies the entire test family of Step 2, so [lem-per-punctual-purity-trait-test] gives punctual purity for every regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible.

source.place: XVI section 3.7, last paragraph, p.255; Proposition 3.5.7.

proof.text: Return to $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. Step 4 applies separately to $X$ and to $Z$, so they satisfy conditions (c) and (b) of [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three]. That statement gives condition (a): the actual Kummer class $\eta_{i,1}:\mathbf F_{\ell,Z}\to i_1^!\mathbf F_{\ell,X}(c)[2c]$ is an isomorphism. Its pointwise classes and its composition convention are exactly those of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], the class used in the item. Step 1 now gives the desired $\eta_{i,n}$ for the original exponent $n$. No field-of-definition or smoothness-over-a-field assumption has entered.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.2.3, p.244; section 3.7, first paragraph; Proposition 3.3.2.

proof.text: For $A=\Lambda_n$ and $m=\ell^n$, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] says the signed Tate sheaves on $Z$ are locally free of rank one, with compatible evaluation. Thus $\Lambda_{n,Z}(c)\otimes\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)\to\Lambda_{n,Z}$ is an isomorphism: on a trivialization it is the ordinary rank-one evaluation. Tensoring with the inverse line and shifting by $[-2c]$ gives $i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}\simeq\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)[-2c]$. With the cochain convention, $\mathcal H^q(K[m])=\mathcal H^{q+m}(K)$, so the right side has only $\mathcal H^{2c}=\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)$. All constructions commute with open restriction by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], so different locally constant values of $c$ are treated on their respective components. For $c=0$ its specified class is the open-and-closed restriction map, including the identity as $1$; on the empty subscheme all assertions are vacuous.
